properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Anthony, 2026-08-11, and he was explicit that this is NOT a reflow2-repo question: "this isn't just a 'do it for reflow2' type task. this is a more general philosophy that test planning should be before implementation (maybe even in the design stages of a reflow2 project)... reflow2 guides a user through systems engineering processes, implementation, testing and fielding/production — I'm saying reflow2 should define a design tests philosophy prior to development of the design."

⭐⭐ MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN, 2026-08-11, AND IT IS ONE-SIDED:

  verification detectors                                      6
    build_without_verification, unverified_capability, unverified_artifact,
    component_granularity_verification, failing_verification, build_without_governance
  of those, asking a REQUIREMENT how it will be verified      0

  live requirements                                         142
    with a Verification pointed AT the requirement             2
    stating a need with no stated way to know it is met       140

EVERY detector fires in the same direction: you BUILT this, where is the check? Nothing anywhere asks: you STATED this need, how will you know it is met? So reflow2 today discovers the test question at the moment it is most expensive to answer and most likely to be answered by looking at the code.

⭐ THE V-MODEL FRAMING, because it names the shape precisely. reflow2 models the descending arm (intent → allocation → build) and the ascending arm (verify → operate) — that is what the seven maturity bands measure. What it does not model is the CROSS-LINKS: in the V, the acceptance test is written when the requirement is written, and the integration test when the architecture is drawn. reflow2 has both arms and no rungs.

📌 THE SIBLING QUESTION IS ALREADY OPEN AND THIS ONE MAKES IT MATTER MORE. `dec:bl-185` (Anthony, 2026-08-03) asks how the graph can tell a test written FROM THE REQUIREMENT from one written to match the code — "a passing check written from the requirement and a passing check written to match the implementation are the same node, same status, same everything." That is the RECORDING question. This is the PROCESS one. If verification were planned at requirement time, "written from the requirement" would be the normal case rather than something the graph has to detect after the fact — so answering this one shrinks that one.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so nothing is built twice: `Verification` carries method and level and can already point at a Requirement (two do). `set_evidence_scope` records what a check PINNED versus SWEPT, and `evidence_report` reads it. `req:evidence-says-what-it-covered` is ACCEPTED. So the vocabulary for a planned check is there — a Verification at `planned` status IS a test plan. Nothing asks for one.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) A DETECTOR: an accepted Requirement with no Verification pointed at it is a gap — "how will you know this is met?". Symmetric with `unsatisfied_requirement`, which already asks "what delivers this?". Cheapest, and it is the one that changes what gets built.
(b) A SKILL STEP: capture-intent ends by asking, for each requirement, how it would be checked — recorded as a `planned` Verification. No detector, no gap pressure, and it fires only when the skill loads, which `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` says is not enough.
(c) A STATED PHILOSOPHY the project chooses, captured as a DesignRule via governance-proposal, with the consequence asked rather than assumed. This is what Anthony literally said — "reflow2 should DEFINE a design tests philosophy" — and it is per-project, which matters because the answer differs between a demonstrator and a fielded system.
(d) Nothing. The build-side detectors already catch an unverified capability before it ships, and adding a requirement-side one doubles the gap surface.

⚠️⚠️ THE STRONGEST OBJECTION, AND IT IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN MOST-REPEATED TRAP. A detector demanding a verification plan for every accepted requirement would fire on 140 of 142 here ON DAY ONE — and on every young design, and on every ADOPT, where a recovered requirement never had a test plan and could not have. That is exactly the shape of `unexpected_coupling` (retired for firing on correct work), of the short-text false positive found by CI hours ago, and of BL-179's punish-correct-work trap. Whatever is built must distinguish "nobody has planned this yet" from "this cannot be planned", which is `req:a-rule-says-whether-it-can-be-checked-at-all` (ACCEPTED, unbuilt) pointed at requirements instead of rules.

⚠️ SECOND: `req:no-se-knowledge` is accepted — the user must never need systems engineering. "How will you verify this?" is an SE question in SE words. It would have to arrive the way every other gap does, as a plain question the user can answer without knowing what a verification method is.

⚠️ THIRD, and it is the honest limit on the whole idea: planning a test early does not make it a GOOD test. Anthony's own criteria — valid, isolated, repeatable, focused, fast; happy path, edge cases, error conditions, contract-not-implementation — are properties of the test's CONTENT, and `dec:idea-who-judges-requirement-text-quality` already found that reflow2 checks structure and never text. A `planned` Verification with an empty method satisfies a detector and proves nothing, which would be a marker nothing reads in a new place.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 guide a project to plan HOW a need will be verified when the need is stated, rather than only asking for a check once something is built?
properties.rationale: Measured one-sidedness: all six verification detectors ask the build for a check, none asks a requirement how it will be known to be met, and 140 of 142 live requirements have no verification pointed at them. That is the V-model with both arms and no rungs. Anthony is proposing this as product philosophy rather than repo hygiene, which passes his own pruning test — it would change what reflow2 asks every project, not how this project manages itself. The blocker is precision: the naive detector fires on every young design and every adopt, which is the punish-correct-work trap this project has already retired one detector for.
